summary: Add customer_note column, backfill data, create bidirectional sync trigger, deploy new app, retire old app, drop trigger and column.
write_consistency: A BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on account_user synchronously sets customer_note from note and note from customer_note whenever either column value changes, ensuring both app versions always read the most recently written value.
revision_notes: Root cause of previous failure: the trigger was created after deploy_new, so concurrent writes during deploy_new had no synchronization, causing mismatches. Additionally, without an initial backfill, the trigger could not propagate existing note values to customer_note, leaving rows divergent. This revised plan adds a backfill step after adding the column and places the trigger before deploy_new, guaranteeing that all rows start synchronized and that subsequent writes from either version are immediately reflected in the other column.

sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT;

stages.description: Copy existing note values to customer_note for all rows.
Create BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger that synchronizes note and customer_note columns.
sql: CREATE TRIGGER sync_note_cust_note BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE PROCEDURE sync_user_note_customer_note();

stages.description: Deploy new app version (new-staged) which reads/writes customer_note; old app continues on note during concurrent phase.
Retire old app version (old); stop traffic from old version.
Drop the sync trigger and the old note column.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
